newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - ITALY - WEDNESDAY, JULY 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - ITALY - WEDNESDAY, JULY 2.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Italian president Oscar Luigi Scalfaro said he was considering keeping his office as president provided he was backed by a very strong political majority (all).

* The board of Banco Ambrosiano Veneto has approved a plan to boost its capital by up to 6.8 trillion lire over five years in preparation for a takeover of 100 percent of the banking assets of saving bank Cariplo (all).
* Telecom group Stet and U.S. giant AT&T are expected today to sign a cooperation deal and unveil detail of their alliance (all).

* Silvio Berlusconi's Fininvest group saw its profits slow by more than six percent last year, after extraordinary items boosted results in 1995, but the media group said it had managed to eliminate its debts in 1996. (all)
* State rail company Ferrovie dello Stato said it saw its loss rise to about five trillion lire in 1997 against 3.84 trillion lire in 1996 (all).
* Fitch, a major U.S.-based debt rating agency, said it has assigned 'AA-' rating to the Republic of Italy's foreign currency debt and 'AA' rating to its local currency debt (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
